question: For high values 15..23 used as the second input data word in exactly the same 36 payloads, does training r2 (high becomes a second answer word) vs r1 (high is input-only) improve accuracy on unseen low partner s5, at matched r1/r2 target counts and total updates?
single_factor: For same 36 high-second raw data payloads (s,v,0,0) and 36 ordinary-low payloads, swap only which payload class is assigned echo r2 rather than r1. Each arm sees identical 120 data payloads, 60 r1 and 60 r2, 1200 target-prefix pairs/epoch, identical model initialization, optimizer, shuffle permutations, updates. The r field and target labels necessarily differ; this is a curriculum-target-assignment intervention, not identical raw Q bits.
profile: SLE-AE1-n5-v1; Q='01'+'010'+r as 3 bits+'0'+a+b+c+d (each 5 information bits + trailing zero)+END '111100'; 39 raw bits. Ordinary token IDs 0..29; END30/UP31 are reserved controls. Answer first r six-bit tokens then external S; r in 1,2. Learner sees only raw Q and teacher-forced correct prefix during supervised training; teacher is deterministic offline label generator, no language model oracle.
base_split: 36 (a,b) low pair IDs0..5. (a+b)%6==0 heldout val 6 pairs; ==1 heldout test 6 pairs; other 24 pairs train; both r1 and r2 for each, c=d=0. Base train 48 Q and 480 target tokens per epoch.
additional_train: 36 high-second payload (a=s0..3,b=v15..23,c=d=0) plus 36 low-only payload selected from 24 base-train low pairs, duplicate-free using c=0 for first 24 and c=1 for latter12. HIGH_OUTPUT high payload r2, low payload r1; HIGH_INPUT_ONLY high payload r1, low payload r2. 72 additional Q, 720 targets per epoch, no test/val high s4/5 in train.
high_val: r2 (s=4,v15..23,0,0), 9 Q, never trained in either arm; analogous domains already inspected in earlier studies, thus not researcher-blind
high_test: r2 (s=5,v15..23,0,0), 9 Q, never trained in either arm; inspect only after training, not new researcher-blind numeric range
additional_diagnostics: 36 high-second training values under r1 and r2, 36 low control items under r1 and r2, all base train/val/test, correct first word, second word, STOP, free-generation failures, all raw bits saved for all models.
model: fresh 160 input one-hot (80 slots x two states), tanh hidden64, 3 logits (0/1/S), 10499 trainable parameters; torch Adam lr0.003, clip grad norm1, batch64; same initial params per seed between arms.
shuffle: numpy.default_rng(seed+97000+epoch).permutation(1200); exactly same ordering in both arms for each seed; no early stopping, no post-test tuning
prerun_gate: PR36 runner sha exact; 39-bit native Q and correct STOP fixture; identical sorted (a,b,c,d) multiset per arm; 60r1/60r2 and 1200 targets each; no high s4 or s5 exposure in train; no low base val/test payload contamination; 10499 param initial network.
fitting_gate: HIGH_OUTPUT must correctly generate at least 30/36 exposed high-r2 training examples AND >=44/48 base train per seed; HIGH_INPUT_ONLY must get >=44/48 base train per seed; otherwise treat as insufficient fitting and no positive transfer mechanism claim.
primary_success: Only if fitting gate passes: each seed HIGH_OUTPUT high-r2 test s5 at least 5/9 AND paired HIGH_INPUT_ONLY at most 2/9; otherwise report partial/negative without new updates or seeds.
interpretation_limit: Only causal effect of matched-payload r/target-assignment policy in this architecture. Model sees different r bits, output lengths and target histories; cannot isolate neuron internals nor claim any general SLE advantage. Val/test low partners 4/5 were discussed previously, thus not a new researcher-blind protocol.
